title: Python Stream Guardian: patterns for graceful checkpointing, resume, and metrics
creator: Arielle Kim
description:
Problem: customers using long-running streaming chat completions encounter partial outputs, spiky network failures, and difficulty resuming sessions without duplicating tokens or losing telemetry fidelity. Current SDK surface provides low-level event callbacks but lacks a composable, testable pattern for checkpointing, idempotent resume, and observable handoff metrics.

Goal: deliver a lightweight Python API (StreamGuardian + SessionCheckpoint) and supporting patterns that make graceful resume and at-most-once delivery ergonomics straightforward for application code while preserving observability and retry semantics. Include examples, unit/integration tests, and a short migration guide.
acceptance_criteria: New StreamGuardian context manager available in py-sdk v2.4.0 with methods: start(), checkpoint(token_index), resume(checkpoint) and close().
Resume is idempotent: repeated resume attempts do not replay previously-acknowledged tokens when the app uses checkpoint() correctly.
SDK emits structured telemetry events for guard_checkpoint, guard_resume_attempt, guard_resume_success, guard_resume_failure with correlation_id and latency_ms.
Integration test covering simulated network failure + resume that asserts no duplicate user-visible tokens and correct checkpoint advances.
Developer docs and a migration example (chat handler before/after) published in the py-sdk docs site.
Benchmark: resume median latency <= 120ms on local CI for 100 token checkpoint payloads; memory overhead <= 5% compared to existing streaming consumer in standard scenario.
design_notes:
Key idea: keep API minimal and composable. Provide a StreamGuardian wrapper that manages a small on-disk (configurable) checkpoint store (default ephemeral in-memory for serverless). It does not force a persistence strategy; instead it exposes checkpoint hooks so platform teams can plug Redis, S3, or local file. Resume is implemented by transmitting 'resume_token' client-side to the service which validates the KV-cache position. Fallback policy: if resume fails, caller can opt-in to either restart-from-beginning or fail-fast. We opt for fail-fast default to avoid silent duplication.

Trade-offs considered:
- Persisting entire KV cache vs token index: storing token index is simpler, smaller, but less robust for model-side recomputation; chosen to start with token index and metadata to minimize memory footprint.
- Automatic vs explicit ack semantics: explicit checkpoint() keeps semantics clear for callers; we provide a convenience auto_checkpoint(interval=...) but mark as alpha.

API surface: StreamGuardian(session_id, checkpoint_store=None, auto_checkpoint=None, on_signal=None) as context manager. session_id is required for telemetry correlation.

Security: checkpoint data is user-controlled; we do not store PII in checkpoints. Document guidance to encrypt external persistence.
implementation_plan: 1) Add StreamGuardian class and in-memory checkpoint store abstraction in sdk/streaming/guardian.py (unit tests).
2) Add persistence adapter interface with two sample adapters: InMemoryAdapter and FileAdapter (no external deps).
3) Implement telemetry hooks and emit structured events to existing telemetry pipeline (ENG-271820 integration).
4) Wire resume protocol to client request metadata: add resume_token header and validate server responses in streaming layer.
5) End-to-end integration test harness: simulate transient socket failures and assert resume behavior.
decisions: Use explicit checkpoint() over fully automatic implicit ack to avoid accidental duplicate delivery.
Default persistence will be in-memory for ease; customers can pass adapters for durable storage.
Fail-fast on resume mismatch to make duplication bugs visible; allow opt-in restart semantics for non-critical flows.
Expose minimal convenience auto_checkpoint but mark as experimental (opt-in flag).
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint store adapters (InMemoryAdapter, FileAdapter).
Integration test: controlled socket drop after N tokens; resume with saved checkpoint; assert no duplicated tokens and checkpoint advanced.
Load test: 1k concurrent stream sessions with periodic checkpointing to ensure memory overhead within target.
Fuzz test for malformed resume_token values to assert safe failure and clear error messages.
rollout_plan: Beta release behind feature flag 'stream_guardian' in py-sdk 2.4.0. Enable for 1% of customers via config for 48h, expand to 10% after observability checks, then full release. Provide migration guidance and opt-out by setting checkpoint_store=None.
